mainTopic: Why forgetting שבת and forgetting the מלאכות lead to different numbers of חטאות, and the sources for חילוק מלאכות (שמואל, רבי נתן, רבי יוסי)
overview: The גמרא first asks why the משנה gives one קרבן per שבת to someone who forgot it was שבת, but one קרבן per מלאכה to someone who forgot which acts are forbidden. רב ספרא answers based on what makes the person stop, but רב נחמן rejects this and explains that a קרבן is counted by the number of separate שגגות. The גמרא then asks for the source of חילוק מלאכות, the rule that each אב מלאכה brings its own חטאת. שמואל learns it from 'מות יומת', applying the verse to a שוגג who 'dies' through paying for many קרבנות. The גמרא asks why שמואל does not use רבי נתן's source, and quotes רבי נתן's ברייתא, which counts 39 מלאכות from 'אלה הדברים' and proves separate liability from the verse 'לא תבערו אש'. The answer is that שמואל holds like רבי יוסי, who uses that verse to teach that הבערה is only a לאו. The גמרא then asks why שמואל does not use רבי יוסי's own source, 'מאחת מהנה', which teaches that sometimes many acts count as one and sometimes one counts as many. The word-by-word explanation of that verse begins here and continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Why do the two clauses of the משנה differ?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the רישא gives one קרבן per שבת, while the סיפא gives one קרבן per מלאכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the difference between the first clause and the last clause?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why the משנה gives different rulings in two cases that look alike. In one case a person forgot it was שבת. In the other case he forgot which acts are forbidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the רישא, the person forgot that today is שבת, and he brings one קרבן for each שבת. In the סיפא, he knew it was שבת but forgot the forbidden acts, and he brings one קרבן for each מלאכה. Both people did many forbidden acts in error, so why should the count be different?

keyTerms.meaning: What is different? (asks for the reason behind a distinction)
The first clause of a משנה
The last clause of a משנה

phrases.english: What is different about the first clause
and what is different about the latter clause?
phrases.notes: רישא = forgot it was שבת (one per שבת). סיפא = forgot the מלאכות (one per מלאכה).

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי שְׁנָא רֵישָׁא וּמַאי שְׁנָא סֵיפָא
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason why forgetting שבת gives one קרבן per שבת, while forgetting the מלאכות gives one קרבן per מלאכה.

steps.title: רב ספרא: It depends on what makes him stop
steps.stepSummary: רב ספרא says the count depends on the kind of information that makes the person stop working.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ספרא said: Here (the first case), he stops when he learns it is שבת. Here (the second case), he stops when he learns the work is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ספרא explains the difference by asking what news would make the person stop. In the first case it is 'today is שבת.' In the second case it is 'this act is forbidden.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first case, one piece of news ('it's שבת') stops all his work at once, so it counts as one sin. In the second case, he must be told about each מלאכה separately, so each one counts on its own.

keyTerms.meaning: Awareness; finding out what he did wrong
Stops; holds back from the act
Here... and here (pointing to the two cases)

phrases.english: Rav Safra said:
Here, he stops because he becomes aware that it is Shabbat,
and here, he stops because he becomes aware of the forbidden labor.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The count of קרבנות follows what kind of awareness makes him stop: awareness of שבת (one) or awareness of each מלאכה (many).

steps.title: רב נחמן: Both kinds of awareness depend on each other
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן argues that knowing it is שבת and knowing the work is forbidden always go together, so they cannot explain the difference.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said to him: Does he stop because of שבת for any reason other than the labors? And does he stop from the labors for any reason other than שבת?
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן attacks רב ספרא's answer. He points out that no person stops working for only one of these reasons.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Telling someone 'it's שבת' only stops him if he already knows the work is forbidden on שבת. Telling him 'this work is forbidden' only stops him if he knows today is שבת. Both pieces of knowledge are always needed, so 'what made him stop' cannot be what separates the two cases.

keyTerms.meaning: Is it at all...? (a rhetorical 'surely not')
Except because of

phrases.english: Rav Nachman said to him:
Does he stop because of Shabbat
for any reason other than the labors?
And does he stop from the labors
for any reason other than Shabbat!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב נַחְמָן כְּלוּם פֵּרֵישׁ מִשַּׁבָּת
steps.kashyaTarget: רב ספרא's distinction between awareness of שבת and awareness of מלאכה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Each kind of awareness only works together with the other, so neither one can be the deciding factor.

steps.title: רב נחמן: The offering follows the number of errors
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן explains that the קרבן is brought for the שגגה, so the count follows how many separate errors there were.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רב נחמן said: The offering that the Torah requires, for what is it? For the error. There, it is one error. Here, there are many errors.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן gives his own answer in place of רב ספרא's. A חטאת atones for a שגגה, so we count the errors, not the actions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A person who forgot it was שבת made one single mistake, and all his work flows from that one mistake. A person who forgot the rules of the מלאכות made a separate mistake about each מלאכה. So he has many שגגות and brings many קרבנות.

keyTerms.meaning: An unintentional error, which is what a חטאת atones for
'The Merciful One', meaning the Torah
Many
There... here

steps.whatToRemember: According to רב נחמן, a חטאת is counted by the number of separate שגגות. Forgetting שבת is one שגגה; forgetting the מלאכות is a separate שגגה for each one.

phrases.english: Rather, Rav Nachman said:
The offering that the Torah obligated, for what is it?
For the unwitting error.
There, it is one error;
here, there are many errors.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected answer with a new explanation.
steps.terutzResolutionType: New explanation replacing a rejected one
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The distinction depends on what kind of awareness makes him stop.
steps.terutzMaskana: The distinction depends on the number of separate שגגות, since the קרבן atones for the שגגה.

steps.title: What is the source for separate liability for each labor?
steps.stepSummary: Quoting the משנה, the גמרא asks for the source of חילוק מלאכות.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says he is liable for each and every labor. From where do we know the division of labors?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the משנה's rule and asks for its source in the Torah. This opens a new topic.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even in one period of forgetting, the משנה makes a person liable for each מלאכה separately. The גמרא wants a verse showing that the Torah treats each מלאכה as its own sin.

keyTerms.meaning: Separate liability for each different מלאכה
From where do we know this?

phrases.english: 'He is liable for each and every labor':
From where do we derive the division of labors?

steps.sheelahInformationSought: A Torah source for separate liability for each מלאכה.

steps.title: שמואל: 'מות יומת' means many deaths
steps.stepSummary: שמואל derives חילוק מלאכות from the double wording 'מות יומת'.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל said: The verse says, 'Those who desecrate it shall surely die.' The Torah added many deaths for one desecration.
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל gives a source. He reads the doubled word 'מות יומת' as teaching that one desecration of שבת can bring many punishments.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse uses the doubled phrase 'מות יומת', 'die, he shall die.' שמואל takes this to mean many 'deaths', meaning many separate liabilities, within one desecration of שבת. So each מלאכה counts by itself.

keyTerms.meaning: Those who desecrate it (Shabbat)
He shall surely die (doubled wording)
Added; included more
Desecration

phrases.english: Shmuel said: the verse states:
'Those who desecrate it shall surely die' (Exodus 31:14).
The Torah added many deaths
for one desecration.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The double language 'מות יומת' teaches many liabilities for one desecration.

steps.title: But that verse is about intentional sin
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that 'מות יומת' speaks about מזיד, but a חטאת is brought for שוגג.
steps.simpleTranslation: That verse is written about one who sins on purpose!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges שמואל's source. The verse talks about the death penalty, which only applies to someone who sins on purpose.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Our question is about how many חטאות a שוגג brings. A verse about the death penalty for a מזיד does not seem to teach anything about the קרבנות of a שוגג.

keyTerms.meaning: Intentional sinner
It is written

phrases.english: This verse is written about an intentional sinner!

steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The verse deals with מזיד (death penalty), while חילוק מלאכות for a חטאת is about שוגג.

steps.title: The verse is redundant for intentional sin, so apply it to unwitting sin
steps.stepSummary: Another verse already teaches the death penalty for מזיד, so 'מות יומת' is applied to שוגג, where 'יומת' means paying through money for קרבנות.
steps.simpleTranslation: If it is not needed for intentional sin, since it is already written, 'Whoever does work shall be put to death,' apply it to unwitting sin. And what does 'shall die' mean? He shall 'die' through money.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends שמואל. A different verse already covers the מזיד, so this verse must be teaching about the שוגג.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This uses the rule of 'אם אינו ענין': when a verse is not needed for its plain subject, we apply it to another subject. Since 'כל העושה מלאכה יומת' already teaches the death penalty for a מזיד, 'מות יומת' is moved to the שוגג. For him, 'death' means a money loss: paying for many קרבנות.

keyTerms.meaning: If it is not needed for this subject (apply it elsewhere)
Apply it to the subject of
Unintentional sinner
Money

steps.confusionAlert: 'יומת בממון' does not mean the שוגג is executed or fined by a court. It means he 'pays' by bringing a separate חטאת for each מלאכה.

phrases.english: If it is not needed for the matter of an intentional sinner,
since it is written: 'Whoever does work shall be put to death' (Exodus 35:2),
apply it to the matter of an unwitting sinner.
And what is meant by 'shall die'?
He shall 'die' through money.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Redirecting a redundant verse (אם אינו ענין)
steps.terutzMaskana: It is redundant for מזיד, so it teaches about שוגג, meaning many money costs (קרבנות).

steps.title: Why not use רבי נתן's source?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why שמואל does not learn חילוק מלאכות from the source רבי נתן uses.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let him derive the division of labors from where רבי נתן derives it!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why שמואל needed his own source when רבי נתן already has one. This step sets up the quote of רבי נתן's ברייתא that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a clear source for חילוק מלאכות already exists, שמואל's derivation seems unnecessary. The ברייתא is about to be quoted to show what that source is.

keyTerms.meaning: Let him derive it instead (from another source)
From where it was derived for

phrases.english: And let him derive the division of labors
from where Rabbi Nasan derives it!

steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Another source (רבי נתן's) already teaches חילוק מלאכות, so why use 'מות יומת'?

steps.title: רבי נתן: The 39 labors from 'אלה הדברים'
steps.stepSummary: רבי נתן's ברייתא begins by asking why 'לא תבערו אש' is needed, and derives the number 39 from 'אלה הדברים'.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught: רבי נתן says: 'You shall not kindle fire in all your dwellings on שבת.' Why does the verse say this? Because it says, 'משה gathered the entire assembly of Israel... These are the things... Six days work shall be done.' 'Things', 'the things', 'these are the things': these are the 39 labors that were told to משה at Sinai.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes רבי נתן's ברייתא. First he asks why the Torah singled out lighting a fire. Then he shows that 'אלה הדברים' hints to the 39 מלאכות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'דברים' (plural) counts as 2, and the extra 'ה' adds 1, making 3. The גימטריא of 'אלה' is 36. Together that makes 39 מלאכות. This sets the background for the next question: is a person liable for each one separately?

keyTerms.meaning: Do not kindle fire
Why does the verse need to say this?
The 39 forbidden labors

steps.confusionAlert: The 39 is not stated outright. It comes from counting: דברים = 2, הדברים = 1 more, and the גימטריא of אלה = 36.

phrases.english: As it was taught: Rabbi Nasan says:
'You shall not kindle fire in all your dwellings
on the day of Shabbat': why does the verse need to say this?
Because it is said: 'And Moshe gathered
the entire assembly of the children of Israel
these are the things, etc.
six days work shall be done.'
'Things', 'the things', 'these are the things':
phrases.notes: Count them up: 'things' gives 2, 'the' adds 1, and אלה is 36 in גימטריא, making 39.

phrases.english: these are the thirty-nine labors
that were told to Moshe at Sinai.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: 'אלה הדברים' hints to the 39 מלאכות given at Sinai.

steps.title: Maybe all 39 in one lapse count as one?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא suggests that doing all the מלאכות in one העלם might bring only one חטאת.
steps.simpleTranslation: I might think that if he did all of them in one lapse of awareness, he is liable for only one.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא raises a possible mistaken idea. Maybe all 39 מלאכות done during one period of forgetting count as one sin.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Knowing there are 39 מלאכות does not yet tell us they are separate sins. Maybe they are all one big prohibition, so one שגגה would bring one קרבן.

keyTerms.meaning: I might have thought (introduces a mistaken idea)
One lapse of awareness

phrases.english: I might think: if he did all of them in one lapse of awareness,
he is liable for only one?

steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether all 39 מלאכות in one העלם bring only one חטאת.

steps.title: Plowing and harvesting are listed separately
steps.stepSummary: The verse 'בחריש ובקציר תשבת' names specific מלאכות, which shows they count separately.
steps.simpleTranslation: The verse teaches: 'In plowing and in harvesting you shall rest.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers with a verse that names plowing and harvesting one by one. This shows that individual מלאכות are counted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By naming specific מלאכות, the Torah shows that at least these are not swallowed into one general sin.

keyTerms.meaning: The verse teaches
Plowing
Harvesting

phrases.english: The verse teaches:
'In plowing and in harvesting you shall rest' (Exodus 34:21).

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Naming plowing and harvesting separately shows that separate liability exists.

steps.title: Maybe only plowing and harvesting are separate
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא objects that maybe only the two named מלאכות are counted separately, and all the rest still count as one.
steps.simpleTranslation: But I could still say: for plowing and harvesting he is liable for two, and for all the rest he is liable for only one!
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא pushes back on its own answer. The verse may only prove that the two named מלאכות are separate.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof from 'בחריש ובקציר' only covers the מלאכות that are actually named. The other 37 might still count as one sin together.

keyTerms.meaning: But I could still say
Liable for two (קרבנות)

phrases.english: But I could still say:

phrases.aramaic: עַל חֲרִישָׁה וְעַל קְצִירָה חַיָּיב שְׁתַּיִם,
phrases.english: for plowing and for harvesting he is liable for two,

phrases.aramaic: וְעַל כּוּלָּן אֵינוֹ חַיָּיב אֶלָּא אַחַת?!
phrases.english: but for all the rest he is liable for only one?!

steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The verse only names two מלאכות, so it cannot prove separate liability for all 39.

steps.title: Kindling was singled out to teach about all the primary labors
steps.stepSummary: הבערה was already included in all מלאכות, yet the Torah mentioned it alone. This teaches that every אב מלאכה brings its own liability.
steps.simpleTranslation: The verse teaches: 'You shall not kindle fire.' Kindling was included in the general rule. Why was it taken out? To compare the others to it and tell you: just as kindling is a primary labor and one is liable for it on its own, so too every primary labor brings liability on its own.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא finishes its proof. It answers the opening question of why the Torah mentions lighting a fire by itself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This uses the rule that when an item already included in a general rule is taken out and mentioned alone, it teaches about the whole group. הבערה is mentioned alone to show that it is its own sin. Every other אב מלאכה is compared to it and also counts separately. This is רבי נתן's source for חילוק מלאכות, which is what the גמרא suggested שמואל could have used.

keyTerms.meaning: Kindling a fire
It was included in the general rule
To compare (make a הקש)
A primary category of forbidden labor
On its own

steps.whatToRemember: רבי נתן learns חילוק מלאכות from 'לא תבערו אש'. Since הבערה is an אב מלאכה with its own liability, every אב מלאכה brings its own חטאת. שמואל learns the same rule from 'מות יומת'.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the classic source for counting each אב מלאכה separately, which is the basis of the משנה's rule. It completes the challenge raised in step 9. The next step answers why שמואל does not use this source.

phrases.english: The verse teaches: 'You shall not kindle fire.'
Kindling was included in the general rule,
so why was it singled out?
To compare the others to it and to tell you:
just as kindling is a primary labor
and one is liable for it on its own,
so too every primary labor,
one is liable for it on its own.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the objection of step 13 and completes רבי נתן's derivation.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Every אב מלאכה brings its own liability, learned by comparing all of them to הבערה.

steps.title: שמואל follows רבי יוסי on kindling
steps.stepSummary: שמואל does not learn like רבי נתן, because he holds like רבי יוסי that הבערה was singled out only to make it a plain לאו.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל holds like רבי יוסי, who said: kindling was singled out to teach that it is only a regular prohibition.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why שמואל did not use רבי נתן's source. שמואל holds like רבי יוסי, who uses the הבערה verse for a different lesson.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי נתן used the separate mention of הבערה to prove חילוק מלאכות. רבי יוסי reads the same verse differently: kindling is pulled out to show it carries only a לאו, not כרת or סקילה. Since the verse is already 'used up' for that lesson, שמואל cannot learn חילוק from it.

keyTerms.meaning: He holds like (follows the opinion of)
Kindling a fire, one of the מלאכות of שבת
It was singled out to be just a לאו (a plain prohibition)
A negative commandment with a lighter punishment than כרת or סקילה

steps.confusionAlert: ״ללאו יצאת״ does not mean kindling is permitted. It means kindling is still forbidden, but carries only the lighter punishment of a לאו instead of סקילה or כרת like the other מלאכות.

phrases.english: Shmuel holds like Rabbi Yosei,
who said: kindling was singled out to be only a prohibition.
phrases.notes: Kindling is excluded from the death penalty and כרת.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 9: שמואל does not adopt רבי נתן's derivation from הבערה (quoted in steps 10-14), because he holds like רבי יוסי.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why does שמואל not learn חילוק מלאכות from הבערה like רבי נתן?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: He holds like רבי יוסי, who uses the הבערה verse to teach that kindling is only a לאו.

steps.title: The baraita showing the dispute about kindling
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא records that רבי יוסי says הבערה ללאו יצאת, while רבי נתן says it came to split the מלאכות.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned in a ברייתא: kindling was singled out to be only a prohibition. These are the words of רבי יוסי. רבי נתן says: it was singled out to divide the מלאכות.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to prove that רבי יוסי really holds this view. The ברייתא shows רבי יוסי and רבי נתן arguing about the same verse.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This confirms that there are two readings of the הבערה verse. רבי יוסי reads it as a לאו, and רבי נתן reads it as לחלק. שמואל sides with רבי יוסי's reading.

keyTerms.meaning: It was singled out to divide (each מלאכה is counted separately)

phrases.english: As it was taught: kindling was singled out to be only a prohibition,
these are the words of Rabbi Yosei.
Rabbi Natan says: it was singled out to divide the labors.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Provides the ברייתא source for רבי יוסי's view cited in step 15.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי יוסי holds הבערה ללאו יצאת
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא recording the מחלוקת between רבי יוסי and רבי נתן

steps.title: Then let שמואל learn division from רבי יוסי's source
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges: if שמואל follows רבי יוסי, he should learn חילוק מלאכות from wherever רבי יוסי learns it.
steps.simpleTranslation: But let him learn the division of the מלאכות from the place where רבי יוסי learns it!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on שמואל. רבי יוסי also holds that each מלאכה counts separately, and he has his own verse for it, so why doesn't שמואל use that verse?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier on the דף, שמואל learned חילוק מלאכות from a different source. The question is: if you follow רבי יוסי, why not take רבי יוסי's own source as well? This step sets up the quote of that source, which comes next.

keyTerms.meaning: But let him derive it (a challenge: why not learn it from here?)
Dividing the מלאכות, meaning each one brings its own חטאת
From the place where he derives it

phrases.english: But let him derive the division of labors
from where Rabbi Yosei derives it!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְתִיפּוֹק לֵיהּ לְחִלּוּק מְלָאכוֹת מֵהֵיכָא דְּנָפְקָא לֵיהּ לְרַבִּי יוֹסֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses שמואל's alignment with רבי יוסי (step 15) to ask why he does not adopt רבי יוסי's source for חילוק.
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's choice of source for חילוק מלאכות
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If שמואל follows רבי יוסי, he should use רבי יוסי's verse for חילוק rather than a different derivation.

steps.title: רבי יוסי's source: 'and does from one of these'
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי learns from ״וְעָשָׂה מֵאַחַת מֵהֵנָּה״ that sometimes one brings one חטאת for everything, and sometimes a separate חטאת for each act.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned: רבי יוסי says, ״and he does from one of these״. Sometimes a person is liable once for all of them, and sometimes he is liable for each and every one.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the ברייתא that shows where רבי יוסי learns חילוק מלאכות. This is the source the קשיא says שמואל should use.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse about bringing a חטאת uses an unusual phrase, ״מֵאַחַת מֵהֵנָּה״. רבי יוסי reads it as teaching two cases: sometimes many sins count as one חטאת, and sometimes each sin counts separately. The 'each one separately' case is חילוק מלאכות.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And he does from one of these', from the חטאת verse in ויקרא ד:ב
Sometimes
Liable to one חטאת for all of them together
For each and every one separately

phrases.english: As it was taught, Rabbi Yosei says:
'and he does from one of these,'
sometimes one is liable once for all of them,

phrases.aramaic: וּפְעָמִים שֶׁחַיָּיבִין עַל כׇּל אַחַת וְאַחַת.
phrases.english: and sometimes one is liable for each and every one.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא, רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר: וְעָשָׂה מֵאַחַת מֵהֵנָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the source of רבי יוסי referenced in the קשיא of step 17.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי יוסי has his own source for חילוק מלאכות
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא quoting רבי יוסי's reading of ״וְעָשָׂה מֵאַחַת מֵהֵנָּה״

steps.title: רבי יוסי son of רבי חנינא explains the words
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא explains that the extra letters in ״מֵאַחַת״ and ״מֵהֵנָּה״ teach: sometimes one is many, and sometimes many is one.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא said: What is רבי יוסי's reason? The verse could say ״one״ but says ״from one״; it could say ״these״ but says ״from these״. This teaches: one that counts as many, and many that count as one.
steps.whatsHappening: An אמורא explains exactly how רבי יוסי reads the verse. The extra ״מ״ on each word shows two opposite cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah could have written just ״אחת״ and ״הנה״. Writing ״מאחת״ and ״מהנה״ hints at both directions. Sometimes what is one (one שבת, one period of forgetting) brings many חטאות, and sometimes many מלאכות bring only one חטאת. The גמרא on the next amud spells out which cases these are: knowing it is שבת but forgetting the מלאכות, versus forgetting שבת while knowing the מלאכות.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the reason?
One that is 'these': one case that brings many חטאות
'These' that are one: many מלאכות that bring only one חטאת

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוסי reads ״מֵאַחַת מֵהֵנָּה״ as teaching both directions: one that is many, and many that is one.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Chanina said:
What is the reason of Rabbi Yosei?
'One' / 'from one'; 'these' / 'from these',
phrases.notes: The verse could have said 'one' and 'these' but added 'from'.

phrases.aramaic: אַחַת שֶׁהִיא הֵנָּה, הֵנָּה שֶׁהִיא אַחַת.
phrases.english: one that is many, many that are one.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי חֲנִינָא: מַאי טַעְמָא דְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the textual basis of רבי יוסי's ruling quoted in step 18.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The extra ״מ״ in ״מאחת״ and ״מהנה״ teaches cases where one act counts as many and many acts count as one.

steps.title: Word by word: 'one' means writing 'שמעון'
steps.stepSummary: The breakdown begins: ״אחת״ refers to a complete act, like writing the full name שמעון; ״מאחת״ starts to describe a partial act.
steps.simpleTranslation: ״One״ means writing the full name שמעון. ״From one״ means...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins explaining each word of the verse with an example from writing on שבת. The explanation continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ״אחת״ means a full, complete מלאכה, like writing the whole name שמעון. ״מאחת״ will describe doing only part of the act, and the example continues on the next amud.

keyTerms.meaning: The name 'Shimon', an example of writing a complete word on שבת
'From one': part of a single act

phrases.english: 'One': writing Shimon. 'From one':
phrases.notes: The sentence continues on the next amud.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins a word-by-word application of the reading from step 19.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ״אחת״ refers to a complete act of writing, such as the full name שמעון.
